title: The Verdict of Greywater Bay
premise: Dominic Thornbury, Greywater Bay's night-shift taxi dispatcher, has spent a decade as the town's invisible archivist, overhearing every secret without ever belonging to anyone. When a wealthy stranger prepays a fare and asks him to prevent a murder scheduled for the solstice, Dominic realizes the killer is someone who has used his own dispatch records to plan the crime — someone who knows the town, and Dominic, better than the police do. As he races to identify the victim and the murderer from ten years of filed conversations, Dominic must finally choose between protecting the people who trusted his silence and telling the truth. The climax forces him to bait the killer with himself as the intended victim, and in the aftermath, Dominic trades his invisibility for a real place in Greywater Bay — as the witness who saved a life.
about_author: Noor Okafor is a former small-town radio producer who spent years listening to the unguarded conversations of night-shift workers. She writes mysteries about the quiet people who see everything, and lives within earshot of a harbor.

chapters.title: The Prepaid Fare
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. A silver-haired client books a taxi in advance for a ride that hasn't happened yet, pays triple, and says only: 'Use it to stop a murder on the twenty-first.' Dominic, who prides himself on filing everything and feeling nothing, can't shake the request. The emotional beat is unease — the first crack in his careful invisibility.

chapters.title: Alphabet of Secrets
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. He combs his mental archive of ten years of overheard fares, mapping grudges, affairs, and debts against the solstice date. Three plausible victims emerge. His loyalty to the town's confidences wars with his growing dread. The beat is the thrill and guilt of finally using what he was never supposed to know.

chapters.title: The Passenger Who Wasn't
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. He realizes one of his regular night passengers, a soft-spoken ferry mechanic named Callum, has been asking oddly precise questions about routes and schedules — questions that mirror the killer's likely planning. When Dominic probes gently, Callum deflects with a warmth that feels rehearsed. The beat is creeping suspicion wrapped in false comfort.

chapters.title: What Marisol Knew
chapters.summary: Marisol's POV, a day-shift dispatcher and Dominic's only friend. She noticed the prepaid booking too and warns Dominic that the police already questioned the company after an anonymous tip. Her fear isn't the murder — it's that Dominic's snooping will expose the dispatch logs, and with them, everyone's secrets. The beat is loyalty pressing against truth.

chapters.title: Ten Years of Silence
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV, with flashbacks. We learn why he came to Greywater Bay: he once testified against a friend and lost everything, so he chose permanent invisibility. The prepaid fare feels like history demanding a repeat performance. The beat is a raw reckoning with memory — the past he filed away resurfacing, unalphabetized.

chapters.title: The Solstice List
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. He narrows the likely victim to Edith Vann, the harbormaster whose planned testimony in a smuggling case would destroy three prominent families. He anonymously tips Detective Reyes, who dismisses him — then reveals someone else already called in the same tip, days ago, in Edith's exact phrasing. The killer is ahead of him. The beat is cold panic.

chapters.title: Fare Denied
chapters.summary: Marisol's POV. The company receives a records subpoena, and Marisol covers for Dominic by misfiling the logs — a small betrayal of her own integrity. Meanwhile Dominic discovers the prepaid booking's payment trail leads back to a shell company connected to Callum. The beat is complicity deepening: both friends now have skin in the lie.

chapters.title: Night of the Long Route
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. On the solstice eve, Dominic shadows Edith's taxi route and catches Callum tampering with the harbor gate locks. Confronted, Callum doesn't deny it — he reveals he's been feeding Dominic false leads all along and knows about Marisol's misfiled logs. The beat is the trap snapping shut: the killer has been reading Dominic's file on himself.

chapters.title: The Last Dispatch
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV, climax. Callum forces Dominic to dispatch Edith's taxi to the harbor at midnight, using Marisol's job as leverage. Instead, Dominic broadcasts a coded all-drivers alert — his decade of dispatcher's rhythm turned into a weapon — summoning Reyes and every cabbie in town to the docks. Callum is taken on the pier with Edith's name on his lips. The beat is Dominic choosing truth at last, loudly, publicly.

chapters.title: Greywater, Morning
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV, resolution. In the aftermath, the town learns what its dispatcher knew and forgives most of it; Edith thanks him, Marisol keeps her job, and Dominic testifies without flinching. He finally accepts the silver-haired client's fare — a ride to the harbor at sunrise, no destination needed. The beat is belonging earned: the invisible man, seen.
